title: Check whether the rotated page root forces a screen orientation
user_impact: Users with fixed-mount screens (e.g. wheelchair-mounted) cannot read the page.
technical_impact: The computed transform (matrix) or rotate of html or body turns by a quarter turn, measured in the audited viewport.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.4 Orientation; ACT b33eff (Inapplicable 4: a rotation in both orientations)
checks.applicability: The root elements html and body of the top document, in each audited viewport: every page has them, so there is no page the check does not apply to.
checks.expectation:
A review when html or body is rotated by a quarter turn in the audited
viewport (computed transform with a rotation component, or the rotate
property; Rendering::box_transform, measured by accessibility::probes), which
turns the whole page sideways, whether set by an orientation media query or
by a script reacting to the orientation. The finding names the rotated
element. Review, not a violation: one snapshot sees one orientation, and a
rotation that applies in both orientations locks nothing; orientation/locked
compares both orientations from the style rules. A full turn (360deg), a
translation or no transform is no rotation. Rotations by a multiple of 180deg
do not swap the axes and are not reported. A page whose computed style cannot
be read records the rule as not run (CapabilityMissing), not as a pass.
